headline: Allowing super access for housing deposits unlikely to improve affordability — more money chasing the same number of assets pushes prices higher and erodes compounding benefits
reasoning: Callum Newell argues that letting younger Australians access superannuation for a home deposit would not meaningfully improve housing affordability. More money chasing the same supply of homes simply bids up prices. He also notes that if the policy becomes a long-term feature, mortgage brokers will factor the super drawdown into borrowing capacity, further inflating prices. Additionally, withdrawing super early sacrifices compounding, which is the core mechanism through which super builds long-term wealth.
